classification.difficultyReason: The hardest demand occurs in b and c: read score labels and cumulative column heights from the histograms, transfer them to tables, then recover individual frequencies by adjacent differences. This links routine procedures explicitly established by the teaching without requiring an unsignposted insight.

content.prompt: Complete frequency distribution tables given these cumulative frequency histograms.

spec.description: Five touching, unfilled orange-outline columns; black arrowed axes; horizontal light-blue grid; c f and x labels.

mathematics.coordinateInterpretation: Half-step boundaries and top-gridline value are reconstruction coordinates, not additional printed givens.

spec.answerVisibility: Histogram and black table cumulative totals are givens; Frequency responses are hidden.

answer.worked:
The cumulative totals are $3,5,8,13,15$. Recover each frequency from the increase in the running total.
$$\begin{align*}f(2)&=3\\f(3)&=5-3=2\\f(4)&=8-5=3\\f(5)&=13-8=5\\f(6)&=15-13=2\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Read scores $18,19,20,21,22,23$ and cumulative heights $2,7,13,16,19,20$. Subtract consecutive cumulative totals.
$$\begin{align*}f(18)&=2\\f(19)&=7-2=5\\f(20)&=13-7=6\\f(21)&=16-13=3\\f(22)&=19-16=3\\f(23)&=20-19=1\end{align*}$$
